rationale: A 55-year-old male with 1-year bilateral hand DIP arthralgia and elbow inflammation was evaluated under a hospital ophthalmologic protocol for patients with suspected chikungunya infection and had an unverified past history of chikungunya fever. step10_contradiction_notes: Initial empiric clinical diagnosis of chikungunya was made at a rural clinic without any laboratory testing; the patient rapidly progressed to seizures, hemothorax, hepatic failure, shock, and death, with IgM and IgG serology confirming Rickettsia spp. infection.
rationale: A 9-year-old boy in rural Mexico with dog/tick exposure presented with high fever, rash, and subsequent arthralgia and was initially diagnosed clinically with chikungunya without any laboratory testing. He deteriorated with seizures, severe thrombocytopenia, bilateral hemothorax, and fatal multi-organ failure, and IgM/IgG serology confirmed Rickettsia spp. Because the initial chikungunya impression relied solely on E3 symptoms without chikungunya-specific laboratory testing and was superseded by confirmed rickettsiosis, VPD is not satisfied -> UNRESOLVED.
